Pilchicocha greets visitors with dark water and reflections of the rainforest. The lake lies in the Ecuadorian Amazon, in the Napo River area, near Sacha Lodge. After traveling along the river and through the forest, its open water feels expansive: you can take in entire treetops above the lake and watch the clouds change their reflections.

The lake is especially rewarding to explore from the water. During a peaceful canoe trip, it is easier to spot birds moving along the shore and listen to the sounds of the forest. A guide helps visitors notice details hidden within the seemingly continuous green wall. Morning and evening light create entirely different impressions of the same lake.

Pilchicocha appeals to travelers who want to spend several days in the Amazon and experience the forest at different times of day. It is pleasant to alternate outings with short pauses by the water: watching ripples left by a paddle, waiting for a bird to appear on a branch or observing the changing light. The lake becomes part of an encounter with the living forest, where every outing unfolds differently.

## Pinar del Río — a Picturesque Corner of Cuba

Pinar del Río was one of the last major Cuban cities founded by the Spanish: it received city status only in 1867. Many Filipinos arrived in the area via Mexico aboard the Manila galleons, so these lands were originally known as Nueva Filipinas. After Mexico gained independence, trade aboard the Manila galleons came to an end, and the same tobacco varieties once exported from the Philippines began to be grown in this part of Cuba. The city that emerged in the heart of the tobacco-growing region became the center of the cigar industry.

If you have ever wondered where the production of the world's finest cigars begins, the answer is the cultivated tobacco plantations of Cuba's westernmost province, Pinar del Río. Yet the plantations are only part of the area's appeal. Its remarkable mogotes — rounded limestone hills rising above flat plains — create landscapes that rival any in the world. These plains, where Cuban cowboys roam and picturesque villages are tucked away, are surrounded by mountain ranges crowned with extensive stretches of tropical forest.

## What Awaits Visitors in Pinar del Río

In Pinar del Río, visitors are introduced to the stages of tobacco production, from the leaf to the packaging. The Francisco Donatién Tobacco Museum is nearby. The province also contains the Viñales Valley and the "Indian Cave", a series of grottoes with rock paintings.

In the Pipo River valley, water runs over a rocky bed through southern forests. The river is among the natural features visitors encounter on excursions to Tierra del Fuego National Park.

The park has a designated access area to the river, and its waterfall is also mentioned among the natural attractions. The riverbank and surrounding forest offer a view of Tierra del Fuego's cool woodland landscape. Independent walks and stops depend on the chosen route.
